chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the man who plays with his wife in the month of Ramadan until he ejaculates. He said, 'Upon him is like what is upon the one who has intercourse.'
If the man ejaculated from looking or from speech without physical contact, there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.يَعْبَثُ: plays or engages in playful intimacy

ai.seo_question: What breaks the fast if a man plays with his wife during Ramadan?
ai.summary: In this narration from Sahih al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that playful intimacy leading to ejaculation carries the same expiation (kaffarah) as full sexual intercourse, emphasizing the severity of breaking the fast in Ramadan. However, he distinguishes this from non-physical acts like looking or speaking, which do not break the fast, highlighting the Shia juristic focus on the mechanism of ejaculation rather than mere proximity. This ruling underscores the balance between marital affection and ritual purity during the holy month.
